# Forecasting a second Wikipedia attack judgment from the first worker's category choices

## Source and alignment

Use Wulczyn, Thain and Dixon's [Wikipedia Talk Labels: Personal Attacks, version 6](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.4054689.v6), released under [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Use its official individual ratings (Figshare file 7554637) and comment split metadata (7554634), pinned in sources.sha256. No answer-equivalence, essay, SNLI or MultiNLI data enter the fit. No new judgments are collected. Read comment text solely to identify duplicates. Use no text, worker IDs, worker demographics or metadata as forecast features.

Align the AE source reader's final vote with the Wikipedia first worker's released binary `attack` flag. Align the richer representation with the same first worker's tuple of `quoting_attack`, `recipient_attack`, `third_party_attack`, and `other_attack` in that order. Key the tuple jointly with the binary vote so the information always nests the binary comparator. Predict `attack` for another worker on that comment. The tuple encodes subtype selections, with no evidence of an ordered path through prompts. In AE, the path separates negative-vote reasons. Here, given the documented coding, subtype detail primarily distinguishes positive votes. This is transfer of the estimator and of the rich-versus-coarse representation question. Wikipedia rates personal attacks, with no shared label meanings or transferable AE probabilities. [Publisher schema](https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Research:Detox/Data_Release#Schema_for_attack_annotations.tsv) · [AE comparison](../decision_paths/design.md)

## Eligibility and item groups

Verify the source digests and expected headers. Require unique revisions in the comments table, only the official train, dev and test split values, integer revision and nonnegative worker IDs, literal binary ratings, and an exact revision join. Audit row-level discrepancies between `attack` and the OR of the four flags. The official binary field remains authoritative and any discrepant tuple stays keyed by its explicit vote. Drop redundant copies of identical (revision, worker, five flags) records. If a worker has conflicting records for one revision, exclude all of that worker's records for that revision before pairing. Require at least two distinct remaining workers.

Use revision as the item. Group comments by exact normalized text with Unicode NFKC, case folding, replacement of the publisher's NEWLINE_TOKEN and TAB_TOKEN markers with spaces, and whitespace collapse. Before any panel-size filtering, exclude every revision in a group that spans more than one official split. Preserve all within-split repeats as separate items and cluster their losses by group. Audit split identities, group counts, cross-split exclusions, worker overlap, singleton/empty panels and final pair counts. The release lacks a talk-page or conversation key. Exact normalized text grouping addresses exact copies under this normalization. The resulting design can include related comments and recurring workers. Inference conditions on the observed worker pool.

## Estimation and comparisons

Use all ordered distinct-worker pairs for an eligible item. Each item contributes one unit of mass, evenly divided over its pairs, in fitting and scoring. For vote x let b(x) be its empirical conditional second-positive probability. For signature s with vote x and training masses n(s) and y(s) (total and second-positive), predict (y(s) + 2b(x)) / (n(s) + 2). Two pseudo-items, binary-centered shrinkage and clipping to [.01, .99] carry over unchanged from the AE experiment.

Use official cleaned train to fit candidate tables for comparator tuning. In dev, choose the strength from {0, .25, 1, 2, 8, 32, 128, 512, 2048, infinity} by lowest item-weighted Brier, breaking exact ties in favor of larger strength. Infinity gives b(x). Use binary backoff for unseen signatures at all finite strengths. For the final frozen candidate and every fitted comparator, refit counts on cleaned train plus dev, then score cleaned official test once. Compare with the dev-tuned smoother, empirical binary conditional and unsmoothed signature table. Also report empirical training marginal and repeating the first vote. Clip all predictions, including controls, to the same interval. Use no test labels to fit or select a forecast. Preserve the dev grid, final fitted cells, test support and scores for every comparator.

## Outcomes and uncertainty

Mean item-weighted Brier is primary. Natural log loss is secondary. Report signed differences (fixed smoother minus comparator), with a cluster-robust standard error over test normalized-text groups conditional on the final tables and realized workers. If there are G groups and N items, use sqrt(G/(G−1) × sum over groups of (sum of item differences in group − group size × overall mean difference) squared) / N. The two prespecified Brier contrasts against binary and dev-tuned smoothing receive Bonferroni simultaneous 95% confidence intervals using normal critical values. Other Brier and log contrasts receive marginal 95% intervals. Report group and pair counts, test mass by signature and descriptive differences for the first-vote strata. Retain ties, losses and rare signatures. A result against the binary comparator addresses incremental information. A result against the tuned smoother addresses choice of regularization. The endpoint is another archived worker's decision conditional on the annotations and sampling design.
